excerpt: The roads behind the Grand Strand's worst crashes, what federal crash data actually shows about seasonal risk, and your rights after a wreck.
keyTakeaways: The Myrtle Beach area's 20+ million annual visitors transform the Grand Strand into one of South Carolina's most dangerous driving environments. U.S. 17 carries more fatal crashes than any other Horry County route (39 between 2020 and 2024, per federal data), and summer is not the deadliest season — 22.6% of fatal crashes fall in June through August, below an even spread. The U.S. 501/Carolina Forest Boulevard intersection leads the region in crashes. South Carolina's three-year statute of limitations (S.C. Code § 15-3-530) and comparative fault rule (less than 51% at fault) protect victims, including out-of-state tourists injured on Grand Strand roads.

faqs.question: What is the most dangerous road in the Myrtle Beach area?
faqs.answer: U.S. 17 (Kings Highway) carries more fatal crashes than any other route in Horry County — 39 between 2020 and 2024, against 23 on U.S. 501, according to NHTSA federal crash data. Running through the heart of Myrtle Beach and the entire Grand Strand, it combines heavy tourist traffic, hundreds of commercial intersections, and frequent pedestrian crossings.

faqs.question: What is the most dangerous intersection in Myrtle Beach?
faqs.answer: The intersection of U.S. 501 and Carolina Forest Boulevard is one of the most dangerous in the entire Myrtle Beach metro area, producing 65% more car accidents than the second-most hazardous intersection. Other high-risk locations include U.S. 501 at S.C. Highway 31, Highway 17 Bypass at Farrow Parkway, and Oak Forest Lane at Pine Island Road.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a car accident lawsuit in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Under S.C. Code § 15-3-530, you have three years from the date of your accident to file a personal injury lawsuit in South Carolina. If you are a Georgia resident injured in Myrtle Beach, be aware that Georgia's deadline is only two years under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33.

faqs.question: Are Myrtle Beach roads more dangerous in summer?
faqs.answer: Not for fatal crashes. Federal data for 2020–2024 shows 22.6% of Horry County's fatal crashes fell in June through August — below the 25% an even spread across the year would give, and below South Carolina's 26.1%. Summer brings far more traffic, unfamiliar drivers and pedestrian activity and produces more crashes overall, but the fatal ones are spread across the calendar, with October, May and December the worst months.

faqs.question: Can I file a claim if I was a tourist injured in a Myrtle Beach car accident?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you are an out-of-state visitor injured in a Myrtle Beach car accident, you generally file your claim in South Carolina where the accident occurred. Your home state's uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage may also provide additional protection. An attorney experienced in cross-state claims can evaluate all available coverage options.

faqs.question: Can I still recover compensation if I was partially at fault for the crash?
faqs.answer: Yes. South Carolina follows a modified comparative fault rule that allows recovery as long as you are less than 51% at fault. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of responsibility. Georgia applies a similar rule with a slightly stricter threshold of less than 50% at fault under O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33.
